asks: How is a conversation recognised in each provider's traffic?
answer: By its content, to find out on captured traffic of each program Silo offers, before a budget on a conversation is offered for it. The providers' APIs keep no conversation, so each request carries the whole conversation so far. A request continues a conversation when its messages begin with an earlier request of that conversation and the reply to it, compared as the provider's format reads them, leaving out what a program changes from request to request, such as cache markers, and what it rewrites in its own history. Tool calls are compared by their id and name. So a retry, a request that goes back to an earlier turn, and a request sent to another model, as a program does when it falls back to one, stay in their conversation: each turn's model is a fact of that turn. Any other request starts a new conversation. When a request names an earlier reply itself, as OpenAI's API allows, that link is followed. A program that shortens a long history, as Claude Code does when it compacts, starts a new conversation by this test. The two are joined, and a budget on the conversation follows the join, only when both requests carry the same session identifier of the program. That join is exact about the identifier only: a program that changes its identifier starts a new conversation, which starts again at zero, as `what-a-conversation-budget-promises` says. A conversation belongs to one computer: the same conversation continued in a fork is a new conversation of the fork.

sets.means: A sequence of turns, in which the model may change from one turn to the next.
